newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai raw premiums supported by China, South Korea.
newsitem.headline: Thai raw premiums supported by China, South Korea.

text.p: Thai raw sugar premiums edged up slightly this week due to offtake from South Korea and news of limited purchases from China, while the whites market remained dominated by Indonesia, trade sources said on Thursday.
Traders told Reuters they expected to see shipments of two to three more cargoes of sugar to China between late this month and mid-April.
South Korea has bought around 10 cargoes, mostly raws, since late last month.
Two cargoes were shipped at end-February while three cargoes were being loaded at Thai ports.
More ships have declared to arrive between now and mid-March to load five to six additional cargoes for shipment to Korea. Suppliers included Mitsubishi, Mitsui, Tate & Lyle and Taiyo.
"These liftings helped boost premiums a bit. But we don't expect any substantial increase until China enters the market with big orders," said a trader with a Japanese house.
"As for buying from South Korea, there is nothing exciting or extraordinary. They purchased a lot but they did the same last year."
Thai raw sugar premiums for March/May delivery were quoted at 0.30/0.40 cents per pound over New York futures on an FOB basis versus 0.25/0.35 cents a week earlier.
May/July deliveries were quoted at 0.35/0.45 cents and July/Sepember was bid at 0.50 cents without any offers, trade sources said.
Thailand's sugar production had reached 4.21 million tonnes as of March 4 compared with 4.19 million in the same period last year.

Although the amount surpassed that of the corresponding period in 1995/96, the increase was caused by higher production capacity and not the yield which was still below last year, industry sources said.
Traders said the market was upbeat about the preliminary January export figure which showed the amount rose to 433,195 tonnes from 409,010 tonnes a year earlier.
Indonesia was the biggest buyer for the month, followed by Japan, South Korea and Malaysia.
